source_row.item_data_json: {"options":{"A":"Temporary flattening of the foam dressing under suction, because this finding by itself indicates that hemorrhage is occurring beneath the dressing.","B":"Bleeding or hemorrhage from the wound, because negative pressure wound therapy has recognized bleeding risks that require ongoing clinical monitoring.","C":"Mild operating noise from the therapy unit, because any audible pump sound indicates tissue injury and requires immediate discontinuation of therapy.","D":"Gradual collection of expected wound drainage in the canister, because any drainage during negative pressure therapy represents a treatment complication."}}
source_row.rationale: FDA identifies bleeding and hemorrhage as important risks of negative pressure wound therapy, so ongoing assessment for bleeding remains necessary. Option B identifies the clinically important complication. Option A treats normal dressing contraction under suction as proof of hemorrhage, which it is not. Option C treats ordinary device sound as evidence of tissue injury without a clinical basis. Option D incorrectly labels any expected wound drainage as a complication rather than assessing the amount and character of drainage and the patient.
